raw_case_text: A 63-year-old male with a history of previously treated hepatitis C presented to the clinic with a complaint of left testicular swelling for 3 months. On physical examination the left testicle was significantly enlarged. No clinically palpable lymphadenopathy could be appreciated. Ultrasound scan of the left testicle showed an enlarged testicle. Serology results were negative for HIV, hepatitis B surface antigen, and hepatitis B core antibody. Hepatitis C antibody was positive; however, hepatitis C polymerase chain reaction was undetectable. The remaining laboratory workup including complete blood count, serum lactate dehydrogenase, beta-human chorionic gonadotropin, alpha-fetoprotein, and calcium levels were all within normal limits. Subsequently, he underwent a radical left orchiectomy. His pathology examination showed plasmablastic lymphoma (Figure 1). Tumor cells were positive for CD38, CD 43, CD 45, CD 56, CD 138, MUM1, C-MYC, lambda, and EBER ISH (EBV-encoded RNA in situ hybridization), but were negative for CD2, CD3, CD4, CD5, CD7, CD10, CD15, CD20, CD23, CD30, CD34, CD79a, kappa, PAX-5, BCL-2, BCL 6, cyclin D1, ALK-1, CK IT, EMA, MPO, D2-40, and HHV 8. The proliferation index as indicated by Ki-67 immunohistochemistry was 90%. Cytogenetic analysis revealed noabnormality. Positron emission tomography (PET) scan showed hypermetabolic mediastinal and hilar lymph nodes (Figure 2). There was a relatively symmetric increased medullary tracer activity in the bilateral proximal femurs, favored to represent red marrow reconversion. A bone marrow biopsy with aspirate revealed no evidence of bone marrow involvement. Given the overlap between PBL and PCM, serum-protein electrophoresis, immunofixation electrophoresis, and free light chain done showed no monoclonal protein. He was started on systemic chemotherapy with dose-adjusted etoposide, prednisone, vincristine, cyclophosphamide, and doxorubicin (DA-EPOCH). He was also treated with allopurinol for tumor lysis prophylaxis. After 2 cycles of DA-EPOCH, a repeat PET scan showed increased hypermetabolic activity in the mediastinum consistent with refractory disease. We reviewed the medical liteature and found few reports of cases with improved outcome utilizing multiple myeloma therapies. Accordingly, the decision was made to start salavage systemic chemotherapy with bortezomib, ifosfamide, carboplatin, and etoposide. A surveillance PET scan (Figure 3) obtained at the time of submission was consistent with remission.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 63-year-old male with previously treated hepatitis C virus infection presented to the clinic with a 3-month history of painless left testicular swelling.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Over the 3 months prior to presentation, the patient noticed progressive enlargement of his left testicle without systemic symptoms.
subjective.past_medical_history: History of chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection, previously treated and cured (sustained virologic response).
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for 3-month left testicular enlargement; negative for B symptoms or palpable nodal masses.

objective.physical_examination: Significant enlargement of the left testicle without palpable inguinal or peripheral lymphadenopathy.
objective.routine_investigations: CBC, serum LDH, beta-hCG, alpha-fetoprotein (AFP), serum calcium, SPEP, serum immunofixation, and serum free light chains were all normal without a monoclonal paraprotein. Serologies for HIV, HBsAg, and anti-HBc were negative; anti-HCV antibody was positive with undetectable plasma HCV RNA PCR. Scrotal ultrasound confirmed left testicular enlargement.
objective.advanced_workup: Left radical orchiectomy histopathology and immunohistochemistry demonstrated plasmablastic lymphoma (PBL): tumor cells were positive for CD38, CD43, CD45, CD56, CD138, MUM1, c-MYC, lambda light chain restriction, and EBV-encoded RNA (EBER ISH) with a 90% Ki-67 proliferation index, and negative for CD20, CD79a, PAX-5, ALK-1, and HHV-8 (normal cytogenetics). Staging bone marrow aspirate and biopsy were negative, whereas staging FDG-PET/CT revealed hypermetabolic mediastinal and hilar lymphadenopathy.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Primary testicular EBV-positive plasmablastic lymphoma (PBL: CD138+, CD38+, MUM1+, c-MYC+, lambda+, EBER+, Ki-67 90%, HHV-8-) with mediastinal and hilar nodal involvement in an HIV-negative, HCV-cured 63-year-old male. Following radical left orchiectomy and tumor lysis prophylaxis with allopurinol, the patient had primary refractory mediastinal progression on PET-CT after 2 cycles of first-line DA-EPOCH chemotherapy; switching to myeloma-targeted salvage immunochemotherapy with bortezomib, ifosfamide, carboplatin, and etoposide (B-ICE) successfully induced complete metabolic remission on surveillance PET-CT.
